body.p: Claims 1-19 are now pending in this application. Claims 1 and 16 have been amended. Favorable consideration and allowance of this application is respectfully requested in light of the following amendments and remarks.
I. Drawings Objection

The Drawings stand objected to under 37 CFR 1.83(a) for failing to show every feature of the invention specified in the claims. In particular, the Examiner contends that the limitations of claims 11-13 and 15 regarding how the claimed surfaces and axis are arranged must be shown. See Office Action, p. 2-3.

Applicant refers the Examiner to FIG. 1 of the as-filed application, which is provided below. FIG. 1 clearly illustrates the orientation of antenna arrays 104 and the surfaces of the satellites 101 with respect to each other. A normal axis to the surfaces of the satellites 101 can also be inferred from FIG. 1 itself.
Ica
In light of the above, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the objection to the Drawings.
II. Claim Rejection - 35 U.S.C. §103

Claims 1, 3-7, 14-16, and 18-19 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over "Spacecraft Formation Flying System Design and Controls for Four Nanosats Mission" by Song et al. ("Song") in view of WIPO Publication 1993/009029 to Stuart et al. ("Stuart"). Claim 2 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and further in view of WIPO Publication 2018/037424 to Satak et al. ("Satak"). Claim 9 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and Satak and further in view of U.S. Patent No. 8,334,809 to Nichols et al. ("Nichols"). Claims 10-13 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and further in view of Nichols.

Claim 8 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and further in view of U.S. Publication No. 2018/02514240 to Rettman et al. ("Rettman"). Claim 17 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Song in view of Stuart and further in view of Russian Patent No. 2668378 to Viktorovich et al. ("Viktorovich").

Applicant has amended independent claims 1 and 16 to further distinguish the present invention from the cited art. Independent claim 1 has been amended to define a satellite system comprising a control system configured to dynamically change the configuration and shape of a set of at least three satellites in a formation, where at least two of the satellites each comprises an observation antenna array, by controlling the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set at least partly based on observation data collected by at least one of the observation antenna arrays of the at least one of the satellites in the set to thereby change at least the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the observation antenna arrays of two separate satellites in the formation for improved beam steering operations for tracking an object whose observation data is currently collected.

Similarly, independent claim 16 has been amended to define a method including the step of controlling, by the control system, the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set at least partly based on observation data collected by an observation antenna array of at least one of the satellites in the formation by sending commands to the propulsion system to thereby change at least the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the observation antenna arrays of two separate satellites in the formation for improved beam steering operations for tracking an object whose observation data is currently collected.

Support for the above amendments can be found on page 8, lines 5-18, on page 9, lines 16- 23, on page 10, lines 14-18, on page 1, lines 10-16, on page 4, lines 11-17, and on page 7, lines 3-7 of the as-filed application. Further support can be found in as-filed dependent claims 2, 3, and 8 and as-filed dependent method claims 18 and 19.
Song relates to a spacecraft formation flying system design and control for a mission
involving four nanosats in a predetermined formation and moving in similar orbital planes. The nanosats in the predetermined formation may occasionally drift apart.

This article does not mention anything about antenna array systems and beam steering involving the antenna arrays of a plurality of satellites in a formation. Further, Song does not disclose a formation of satellites with antennas where observation data collected by at least one
of the antennas in the formation may be used for improved beam steering operations and dynamically changing the formation based on the collected observation data.

In particular, Song does not hint to a solution where observation data collected by at least one of the antennas in a formation of satellites may be used for improved beam steering operations by changing the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the antenna arrays of separate satellites in the formation based on observation data collected by at least one of the antennas in the formation.

Song describes a satellite formation with four nanosats where the relative distance between the nanosats can be decreased and increased during along-track and cross-track formations, respectively, via orbit controls in the desired duration. The problem addressed in Song is that nanosats that move along similar orbital planes in a predetermined formation drift apart owing to the difference in orbital drift rate. The drift recovery control can be performed several times because of thrust limitations and control errors. The orbital control for the formation flying system in Song shall maintain the relative distance to prevent the nanosats from passing through each other, see for example column 1 on pages 151 and 152, and the text to Fig.
On page 150, column 2 and FIGS. 3(a)-3(b), Song describes two modes of operation
where the nanosats may be arranged in either along-track formation to collect temporal data or in cross-track formation to collect spatial data.
On page 151, column 1 and FIGS. 4(a)-4(d), Song describes a sequence of four

subsequent types of predetermined phases and orbit controls including a "Launch & Early Orbit Phase", an "Along-track Formation Phase", a "Cross-track Formation Phase" and a "Reconfiguration" phase in which the distance between the rightmost and leftmost satellites along the cross-track direction is increased.
Song thus proposes a few predetermined modes of operation including a first

predetermined along-track formation adapted for collecting temporal data and a (subsequent) predetermined cross-track formation adapted for collecting spatial data. Song addresses the problem that nanosats in a formation that move along similar orbital planes drift apart owing to the difference in orbital drift rate by orbital control using a thrust that maintains the relative distance between the nanosats to prevent the nanosats from passing through each other.

Song is silent to a system and method for improved beam steering operations involving that the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the observation antenna arrays of two separate satellites in a formation including at least three satellites may be dynamically changed.
In particular, Song is silent to a system and method adapted for changing the relative

angle directions of the radiation lobes of the observation antenna arrays of two separate satellites based on observation data collected by at least one of the observation antenna arrays and where the change in the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes is used for improved beam steering operations for tracking an object whose observation data is currently collected.
Amended claim 1 distinguishes over the Song reference by defining a satellite system

comprising a control system configured to dynamically change the configuration and shape of a formation by controlling the propulsion system of the at least one of the satellites in the set by sending commands to the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set at least partly based on observation data collected by at least one of the observation antennas of the at least one of the satellites in the set to thereby change at least the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the observation antenna arrays of two separate satellites in the formation.

Amended method claim 16 distinguishes over the Song reference by defining a method for dynamically changing the configuration and shape of a formation comprising at least three satellites including at least two satellites each provided with an observation antenna array by controlling the propulsion system of the at least one of the satellites in the formation at least partly based on observation data collected by at least one of the observation antenna arrays of the at least one of the satellites in the set to thereby change at least the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the observation antenna arrays of two separate satellites in the formation.

The above deficiencies of Song cannot be cured by the remaining cited art. As the remaining cited art also fails to disclose this aspect of independent claims 1 and 16, no combination of the cited art can be determined to teach that which is called for in independent claims 1 and 16.
Regarding Stuart, it's claims, page 4 and FIG. 1 (as cited in the Final Office Action)

discloses a spacecraft designs for a Satellite Communication System including a hemispherical, high-gain, electronically-steered antenna array (12) that is always pointed toward the Earth (E) and where the interior of the dome-shaped antenna array (12) is used to store solar cell panels
(16) which unfurl through an opening (15) in a space-facing array (18) when the spacecraft (10) reaches its final orbit. Stuart fails to remedy at least the above-underlined deficiencies of Song.
On page 16 and FIG. 4 of Satak (as cited in the Final Office Action), an exemplary

architecture of a space internet network is illustrated and described. The space internet network comprises a Satellite Constellation 401, a plurality of Earth Internet Gateways 402a... 402n and a plurality of User Terminals 403a, 403b, 403c... 403n. The Satellite Constellation 401 comprises a plurality of satellites 401a, 401b... 401n. The Satellite Constellation 401 forms a network in space, that enables a communication between the plurality of satellites 401a, 401b... 40 in and the plurality of Earth Internet Gateways 402a... 402n. Satak fails to remedy at least the above- underlined deficiencies of Song.
Claim 24 and FIG. la of Nichols (as cited in the Final Office Action) discloses an

antenna including a first planar array of antenna elements and one or more side planar arrays of antenna elements, each side array adjacent to the first array and tilted at a predetermined angle relative to the first array. The antenna may also include a plurality of transmit/receive modules, each module coupled to one antenna element. Each transmit/receive module includes phase shifters for varying the relative phases of the antenna elements to form a desired overall beam pattern, and a low noise amplifier and high-power amplifier for amplifying signals received and transmitted by the antenna element, respectively. Nichols fails to remedy at least the above- underlined deficiencies of Song.

Paragraph [0040] of Rettman (as cited in the Final Office Action) discloses a hall effect thruster and a gridded ion thruster using electrostatic actuation for changing the movement and direction of a satellite. Rettman fails to remedy at least the above-underlined deficiencies of Song.

FIGS. 1-3 and 6 of Viktorovich (as cited in the Final Office Action) discloses a spacecraft comprising a radiation sensor. Viktorovich fails to remedy at least the above-underlined deficiencies of Song.

As a result of the above, independent claim 1, as amended, distinguishes over Song, and Song in combination with any and all of the other references Stuart, Satak, Nichols, Rettman and Viktorovich cited in the Final Office Action, by defining a satellite system comprising a control system that is configured to control the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in a formation including at least three satellites at least partly based on observation data received by
the control system from at least one of the observation antenna arrays of at least one of the satellites in the formation.

In particular, amended claim 1 distinguishes over Song in combination with any of the other cited references by defining a control system configured to control the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set at least partly based on observation data collected by at least one observation antenna array to thereby change the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of at least two observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the formation for improved beam steering operations and for the purpose of tracking a moving object whose observation data is currently collected.

Further, independent claim 16, as amended, distinguishes over Song, and Song in combination with any and all of the other references Stuart, Satak, Nichols, Rettman and Viktorovich cited in the Final Office Action, by defining a method for dynamically controlling the configuration and shape of a satellite formation comprising at least three satellites that includes the step of controlling, by the control system, the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set at least partly based on observation data collected by at least one of the observation antenna arrays of the satellites in the formation and that is received by the control system.

In particular, amended claim 16 distinguishes over Song, and Song in combination with any and all of the other references cited in the Final Office Action, by defining a method including the step of controlling, by the control system, the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set at least partly based on observation data collected by at least one of the observation antenna arrays of the satellites in the formation to thereby change the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of at least two antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the formation for improved beam steering operations and for the purpose of tracking a moving object whose observation data is currently collected.

Hence, no combination of the above-mentioned references teaches each and every of the above-underlined distinguishing features and limitations found in claims 1 and 16, or any of the claims that depend therefrom.
In light of the above, Applicant contends that amended independent claims 1 and 16 are patentably distinct from the cited prior art. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests
withdrawal of the rejection of independent claims 1 and 16 under 35 U.S.C. §103, along with all claims depending therefrom.
In light of the amendments and remarks above, Applicant believes the application is in condition for allowance.
